text:
Berkly Catton is the reason to watch the Kraken right now. He has 10 points in his last 10 games (5.7 expected), and his first NHL hat trick in a 5-1 win over Vancouver was a franchise first. His line with Kaapo Kakko and Shane Wright is roughly even on chances, which for a group that young is a good sign.

The team around him is harder to read. Seattle is 10-9-1 and in the race, with our playoff odds at 29%, but it has only 46% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and 45% at 5v5. It has scored about 7.6 more goals than its chances would predict, and by our numbers it has a couple more points than it deserves. That is a thin margin to live on.

Saturday's 4-3 loss in San Jose showed the cracks: down 3-1 after one period, two power-play goals allowed, and coach Lane Lambert calling the penalty kill "the elephant in the room," per the Kraken's Alison Lukan. Matty Beniers has scored in three straight, at least.

The veteran line of Jordan Eberle, Chandler Stephenson and Bobby McMann has been caved in at 5v5 (39% of expected goals), and McMann has 2 points in 10 on 4.9 expected. Adam Larsson and Vince Dunn, the shutdown pair, get only 39% of shot attempts. What we'd watch: whether the young centres take more of those minutes.
